title: Coherent Phonon Generation from Prethermal Carrier Populations in a Semiconductor
authors: Mingyu Shi, Matteo Savoini, Patrick Friebel, Andrea Annunziata, Thomas Metzger, Yunpei Deng, Laura Cattaneo, Steven L. Johnson
abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. Fitting this model to the data yields an excited transition state lifetime of a few femtoseconds. These results identify transition selectivity, rather than a thermalized total carrier density, as a key factor controlling coherent-phonon generation in semiconductors excited near a band gap.
summary: This study analyzes how coherent phonons are generated in semiconductors when excited by ultrafast lasers. By comparing experimental measurements across the band gap with theoretical models, the authors show that the process is controlled by the specific electronic transitions (transition selectivity) rather than the total thermalized carrier density. This highlights the importance of non-equilibrium carrier dynamics in condensed matter response.
main_problem: The paper investigates the physical mechanism governing the generation of coherent optical phonons in semiconductors following ultrafast laser excitation.
main_result: The coherent phonon amplitude depends on transition selectivity, weighted by optical matrix elements, rather than simply on the total thermalized carrier density, contradicting simpler thermal models.
method: The authors combine systematic ultrafast laser measurements across the band gap with first-principles DFT calculations to model the photoexcitation dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a semiconductor (Tellurium) excited by tunable ultrafast lasers near the electronic band gap. The theoretical framework compares thermalized carrier models (DECP) against a transition-resolved prethermal force model.
key_observables: Coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric A1 phonon mode, and the spectral dependence of this amplitude on the excitation photon energy.
important_parameters: Excitation wavelength tuning across the band gap, and the resulting excited transition state lifetime (estimated to be a few femtoseconds).
main_assumptions: The prethermal force model assumes the force is governed by the sum over optical transitions weighted by coupling strengths and transition probabilities.
figures_summary: Figures show the spectral evolution of the coherent A1 response vs. fluence, comparing the measured responsivity against predictions from thermalized models and the successful fit using the prethermal force model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the problem (phonon generation mechanism), testing existing models (DECP theory), demonstrating their failure against spectral measurements, and finally proposing and validating a transition-resolved prethermal force model.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed, first-principles understanding of non-equilibrium carrier dynamics, showing how transient, non-thermalized populations dictate macroscopic material responses like lattice vibrations.
